title.narrative: Deliver life-saving essential health services including emergency health care services and referrals to most vulnerable populations in ongoing conflict zones in Myanmar

description.narrative: I. The overarching operational objectives of the projectDeliver lifesaving essential health services including essential obstetric care, neonatal care, childcare, emergency referral, non-communicable diseases care (hypertension & diabetes), psychological first aid, nutrition, mild, moderate & severe trauma care, cervical cancer screening and prevention services, acute respiratory infections management & common health problems management services to most vulnerable population with ongoing conflicts in the Magway, Mandalay, Sagaing, Tanintharyi Regions, and Kayah, Kayin, Southern Shan and Northern Shan States. Hence, the project will enhance equitable and sustained access to lifesaving essential health service leveraging strategic partnership and innovative response modalities to address the urgent needs of the most vulnerable population in the prioritized areas. It will also help strengthen the health response to acute on-set emergencies through the implementing partner’s network and help reduce avoidable, excess morbidity, mortality, and disabilityII. The sectoral priorities supported will be the following:1. Scaling up the delivery of emergency and lifesaving essential health services, prioritizing the most vulnerable population including emergency care and referral.2. Procurement of essential supplies, medicines and necessary equipment for delivering emergency and basic lifesaving health services.3. Strengthening of surveillance and timely detection and coordinated response to notifications of outbreaks of epidemic-prone diseases.4. Enabling the health workforce to deliver emergency and basic lifesaving health services and monitor service provisionIII. The services will directly benefit 47,110 girls, boys, women and men in Sagaing, Kayah, and Southern Shan States. WHO Myanmar has a well-established partner network including international organizations, CSO and CBOs and EHOs ensures basic and emergency service delivery, disease surveillance and response, as well as the capacity for procurement of necessary medical supplies and equipment to ensure a quality response.IV. Proposed activities: a. Provision of lifesaving emergency and basic healthcare service packages through fixed, mobile clinics and community-based mechanisms, including emergency care and essential medical care for newborns, children, pregnant and lactating mothers, and mental health and psychosocial support.b. Acquisition of critical pharmaceutical supplies and life-saving medical equipment to support the delivery of life-saving emergency and essential healthcare services, including emergency obstetric and neonatal carec. Enhancing surveillance and early warning systems to ensure prompt identification and coordinated actions in response to potential outbreaks of diseases that are prone to epidemicsd. Empowering the health workforce to deliver critical emergency and basic lifesaving health services while ensuring rigorous monitoring of service provision
